statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = max{ t ∈ Z : t <= limit and t != passengers[j] for all j with 0 <= j < m }, where B, S, k, L, limit are defined as follows. Let B = max(buses). Define the boarding assignment by processing buses in increasing order of departure time; for each bus departure d, among passengers with arrival <= d not yet assigned, assign up to capacity passengers with the earliest arrival times. Let S be the set of passengers assigned to the bus departing at B, k = |S|, and if k > 0 let L = max{ passengers[j] : j in S }. Set limit = B if k < capacity, and limit = L - 1 if k = capacity. Equivalently, r <= limit, r != passengers[j] for all j, and for every integer t with r < t <= limit there exists j such that t = passengers[j].
preconditions: Let n = len(buses) and m = len(passengers). The parameters satisfy the problem Constraints: n >= 1, m >= 1, 1 <= capacity <= 100000, 2 <= buses[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n, 2 <= passengers[j] <= 1000000000 for every j with 0 <= j < m, all elements of buses are pairwise distinct, and all elements of passengers are pairwise distinct.
